title: Rise per Step
idea: The gradient of a line is the change in y for each step of 1 in x, the same everywhere along the line.
misconceptions: Computes run over rise, (x₂ − x₁)/(y₂ − y₁), giving the reciprocal of the gradient
Subtracts the coordinates in inconsistent order, (y₂ − y₁)/(x₁ − x₂), and gets the wrong sign

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions; with no prerequisite explainer there is one recall version, so they are the same. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: No prerequisite in the map, so the recall is one tap question on coordinates from earlier school, with no callback line ("builds_on": null).

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. Of the skill's methods, rise over run on a graph is the big idea and the two-point formula is the lesson. Rearranging to y = mx + c and m = −a/b need the equation of a line, which is ex.functions.line-equation, so the third misconception (reading a coefficient of ax + by + d = 0 as the gradient) is left to that script.

The cold open's question (which track is gentler) is answered in example 3(c) and again in the sign-off. Both tracks use the same numbers all the way through: the east track is 12 up over 40 across, which is P(20, 5) to Q(70, 20); the west track is 9 up over 25 across.
The turns use fn-line-from-conditions, whose chain starts with the gradient of a segment. Its fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Signal Tower, this is Rook. Two straight tracks run up the hill to the tower, and my bakkie only makes it up the gentler one.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The east track climbs twelve metres over forty metres across. The west track climbs nine over twenty-five.

board.write: East: up 12 m over 40 m across.   West: up 9 m over 25 m across.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Nine is less than twelve. Does that make the west track gentler? Hold that thought. Over.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: One check first. Tap one.

ask.prompt: Going from (1, 4) to (5, 10), how much does y go up by?

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Six. Ten take away four. Across is four, up is six. Hold on to both.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: y is the second coordinate. It goes from four to ten, and ten take away four is six. Across, it goes from one to five. That's four.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The east track. Start at the bottom, drive forty metres across, and you're twelve metres higher.

board.write: East track: 40 m across, 12 m up

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: How much up for one metre across? Share the twelve over the forty. Twelve over forty is zero point three.

board.write: 12 ÷ 40 = 0.3 m up for each 1 m across

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Zero point three up for every metre across, at the bottom of the track or near the top. On a straight track it never changes.

board.write: the same at every step of the line

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: That's the gradient. The change in y for each step of one in x.

board.write: gradient: the change in y for each step of 1 in x

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The change up is the rise. The change across is the run. Gradient is rise over run, and we write it m.

board.write: rise: change in y.   run: change in x

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Two points on the line, x one, y one and x two, y two. Rise is y two minus y one. Run is x two minus x one, the same order, top and bottom, and it works for any two points you pick, because the gradient is the same everywhere, and that's what straight means. Sorry. Back on frequency.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Up to the right, the gradient is positive. Down to the right, negative. Flat, zero.

board.write: m > 0: up to the right.   m < 0: down.   m = 0: flat.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: My oupa drove his bakkie up this hill backwards once. Reverse was the strongest gear it had. Same hill, same gradient, a lot more shouting.

problem.setup: Find the gradient of the line through A(2, 3) and B(6, 11).

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: On paper. Step one: what we're finding. m, the gradient of the line through A and B.

board.write: Find m, the gradient of the line through A(2, 3) and B(6, 11).
board.label: Step 1: what are we finding?

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step two: the givens. A is the first point, two, three. B is the second, six, eleven.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step three: the formula. m equals y two minus y one, over x two minus x one.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step four: substitute. Eleven minus three on top. Six minus two underneath.

choices: The gradient is the change in y over the change in x
The bigger values go on top
It doesn't matter which is on top

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Copy that. Rise on top. Run underneath.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Rise over run. Eleven and three are y values, so their change is the rise, and the rise goes on top.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Step five: evaluate. Eight over four. The gradient is two. Up two for every one across.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check: from A, four steps across at two up each is eight up. Three plus eight is eleven. That's B.

problem.setup: Find the gradient of the line through C(−1, 7) and D(3, −5).

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Next one adds negatives. The line through C, minus one, seven, and D, three, minus five.

board.write: Find m for C(−1, 7) and D(3, −5).

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The rise first. Minus five take away seven is minus twelve. It goes down.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: The run is yours. Same order: D's x minus C's x. I'll keep the channel open.

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Four. Taking away minus one adds one. Lekker.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: Three take away minus one. Taking away a negative adds, so it's three plus one. Four.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: So m is minus twelve over four. Minus three. Down three for every one across.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check: D is to the right of C and lower, so the line goes down to the right. Negative. Out.

board.write: Check: x goes up, y goes down, so m < 0 ✓

problem.setup: A straight track up to the Signal Tower passes through P(20, 5) and Q(70, 20), where x is the distance across and y is the height, both in metres.

parts.text: Find the gradient of the track.
The track reaches the tower at T(110, k). Find k.
A second track climbs 9 m over 25 m across. Determine which track is steeper. Justify your answer.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Now the way a paper would set it. Back to the east track, with coordinates on it. x is the distance across, y is the height, both in metres.

board.write: P(20, 5), Q(70, 20): x across, y height, in metres

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part a. Rise, twenty minus five, fifteen. Run, seventy minus twenty, fifty. Fifteen over fifty is zero point three.

board.write: The gradient of the track is 0.3.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part b. The track reaches the tower at T, one hundred and ten, k. We want its height.

ask.prompt: Why can we use P and T in the gradient formula?
choices: T is on the same straight track, so the gradient is still 0.3

right.speaker: rook-dead-air
right.say: Ja. Straight line, same gradient, any two points.

not_yet.speaker: rook-dead-air
not_yet.say: T is on the same straight track. The gradient is the same between any two points on a straight line, so P to T is zero point three too.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: From P to T, the gradient is still zero point three. So k minus five, over one hundred and ten minus twenty, equals zero point three.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Ninety across. Multiply both sides by ninety. k minus five is twenty-seven, so k is thirty-two. The tower stands thirty-two metres up.

board.write: The track reaches the tower 32 m up.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Check from Q instead. Forty more across, at zero point three, is twelve more up. Twenty plus twelve, thirty-two.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Part c. Second track: nine over twenty-five is zero point three six. Bigger gradient, more climb for every metre across.

board.write: The second track is steeper: it climbs 0.36 m per metre across, against 0.3 m.

beats.speaker: rook-dead-air
beats.say: Justify means give the reason, so the comparison goes on the board as well. Out.
